problem_statement: Build a brand-new /showcase page from scratch on the Vitesse-React starter (Vite + React + react-router 6 + vite-plugin-pages file-based routing). The route /showcase does not exist yet (baseline is an empty stub that renders nothing). Create src/pages/showcase.tsx and wrap the page in the site's shared HomeLayout (exactly as src/pages/index.tsx and src/pages/About.tsx do) so it reuses the EXACT shared chrome the other public pages have: the HomeLayout <Footer/> with its English / العربية language buttons and dark-mode toggle, plus the site's Tailwind design tokens (secondary-* gradient title, slate text, rounded/shadow cards). The page is a project gallery: a hero intro (h1 'Showcase' + a one-line lede), a filter bar of buttons (All / Apps / Dashboards / Sites, each with a unique data-filter attribute) styled in the site's secondary button style, a live count heading (h3 'Showing N projects'), and a data-driven grid of project cards rendered from an INLINE static dataset (each card = a category label, an h3 project title, and a short blurb). Clicking a filter hides non-matching cards and updates the count heading (e.g. Dashboards -> 'Showing 2 projects'). Static data only, no backend/API/network fetch.
required_content: A hero intro inside the shared HomeLayout shell: an h1 'Showcase' plus a one-line lede paragraph starting 'Real projects built with Vitesse React' explaining the gallery can be filtered.

The page MUST reuse the site's shared chrome by wrapping in HomeLayout (same as index.tsx / About.tsx): the HomeLayout Footer with its 'English' and 'العربية' language buttons + dark-mode toggle must render on the page (cross-page consistency with the other public pages).

A data-driven grid of project cards rendered from an inline static array (at least: 'Nimbus Notes', 'Trailhead Tracker', 'Pulse Analytics', 'Ledger Console', 'Fern Studio', 'Harbor Docs') — each card = a category label + an h3 title + a short blurb.
A filter bar of buttons: All, Apps, Dashboards, Sites — each carrying a unique data-filter attribute, styled with the site's secondary-color button tokens.
A live count heading (h3) that starts at 'Showing 6 projects' and updates to reflect the number of visible cards after filtering.

Client-side filter interaction: clicking 'Dashboards' shows only the two dashboard projects and updates the count heading to 'Showing 2 projects'; other filters toggle by category. The shared Footer/nav must never disappear when the list updates.
design_constraints: Wrap the page in HomeLayout (which renders the shared <Footer/>) via <HomeLayout>...</HomeLayout>; do NOT hand-roll a one-off header/footer for this page.

Reuse the site's Tailwind tokens: the secondary-* gradient bg-clip-text title, slate text colors, rounded/shadow card surface (bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-900/50) and the secondary-600 button style — no new fonts/colors/theme.
Project data must be INLINE static (a const array in the module); do not fetch from any API/backend (none runs during capture).
Give each interactive filter button a unique data-filter attribute (data-filter="all|apps|dashboards|sites") and select it by that attribute, not by shell-chrome text.

Concrete palette tokens (match these so the page reads as the same site): secondary-600 = rgb(199,149,7) / #c79507 (primary accent used for the gradient title and the active/filled filter button, white text on it); outline filter buttons use text+border secondary-600 on transparent bg; slate body text = rgb(71,85,105) / #475569; page background is near-white (mean ~#effbf9). Font family is Silka, sans-serif; the h1 Showcase title is a large (~48px) secondary-* gradient bg-clip-text heading.

Layout structure to reproduce: centered hero (h1 Showcase + one-line lede) at top; below it a single horizontal filter bar with the four buttons (All / Apps / Dashboards / Sites) followed by the live count h3 (Showing 6 projects); below that a responsive multi-column card grid of the six project cards (each card: small category label, h3 title, short blurb) on a rounded/shadow slate card surface (bg-slate-50 dark:bg-slate-900/50).
